commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". Summary of `C:\Users\Public\agentdemo\work\D7-plan_2026-10-20T17-01-46-801Z`. This is a tiny, framework-free prototype of 7 flat files with no package.json, no node_modules, and no git repo. I made no changes.

**Framework and stack**
- It uses plain browser HTML and JavaScript with no bundler or framework.
- The logic modules are CommonJS (`module.exports`) and run under Node.
- There are no dependencies.

**Pages, routes and navigation**
- There is no router, no navigation and no multi-page structure.
- `index.html` is the only real page. It is titled "September expenses" and shows a total in `<span id="total">`. An inline script fetches `data.json` and sums the amounts in cents.
- The "pages" are only described in comments inside the logic modules. None of them has an HTML page yet, and nothing links to anything else.
  - `expenses.js` is the "Expenses page": `total(items)`.
  - `report.js` is the "Monthly report page": `totalsByCategory(items)` returns `{category: total}`.
  - `budget.js` is the "Budget page": `remaining(items, budget)`.
- Adding a page would mean creating a new `.html` file, plus a hand-written nav that does not exist yet. `index.html` would need links added too.

**Spending data, categories and API**
- `data.json` is a flat array of 7 September 2026 records. Each record is `{date: "YYYY-MM-DD", category: string, amount: "NN.NN"}`. Amounts are strings.
- Categories are free-text strings on each record. There is no category table or list. The values are `groceries`, `transport` and `eating out`, so `eating out` contains a space.
- `expenses.db` is an 8 KB file, probably SQLite. Nothing in the code reads it. I did not inspect its contents.
- There is no API or server. The browser reads `data.json` through `fetch("data.json")`, which needs an HTTP server because `file://` would block it. There is no store or state management.
- Money handling is consistent. Every module converts amounts with `Math.round(Number(amount) * 100)`, sums integer cents, then divides by 100. This logic is duplicated in `index.html`, `expenses.js`, `budget.js`, `report.js` and `check.js`.

**Charts**
- There is no chart library and no chart components. `report.js` `totalsByCategory` is the natural data source for a chart.

**Styling**
- There is none. No CSS files, no `<style>` blocks, and no classes.

**Tests**
- `check.js` is a hand-rolled script. Run it with `node check.js`.
- It loads `data.json` and the three modules, then prints PASS or FAIL for three checks: the expenses total, groceries in the report (expected 131.25), and budget remaining against a budget of 300. It exits with code 1 if any check fails.
- There is no test runner, no browser or UI tests, and no tests for `index.html`.

**Implications for a new page**
- You would add a new `.html` file or two, and any chart would need either a CDN script or hand-written SVG. You would also need to introduce navigation between pages.
- For a per-category breakdown chart, reuse `totalsByCategory` from `report.js`.
- To keep the existing test style, extend `check.js`.

# Plan: spending-per-category bar chart page

## Context
The prototype (plain HTML + CommonJS JS, no build, no deps) has one page, `index.html`, showing a September total. `report.js` already exposes `totalsByCategory(items)` (integer-cent safe) but has no page. Goal: a new page with a bar chart of spending per category.

## Approach
- New `report.html`: fetches `data.json`, computes per-category totals, renders a hand-written inline SVG bar chart (no chart library, no CDN, matching the dependency-free style).
- Reuse `totalsByCategory` from `report.js`. It uses `module.exports`, so add a browser-safe guard at the bottom (`if (typeof module !== "undefined") module.exports = ...`) plus a global for the browser, keeping `check.js` working. Load it via `<script src="report.js">`.
- Chart: vertical bars sorted by total descending, category labels on the x-axis (handles "eating out" with a space), value labels on bars, y-axis with a baseline and a few gridlines, currency formatted to 2 decimals. Single colour (one series), accessible text contrast, `<title>` per bar and an `aria-label` on the SVG. Follow the `dataviz` skill when writing the chart code.
- Navigation: add a link from `index.html` to `report.html` and back (the project has no nav yet).

## Files
- add `report.html`
- edit `report.js` (browser-safe export)
- edit `index.html` (link to report page)
- edit `check.js` (optional: assert the chart's data helper, e.g. totals sorted order)

## Verification
- `node check.js` still passes (groceries 131.25 etc.).
- Serve the folder (`python -m http.server` or `npx serve`), open `/report.html`, confirm three bars (groceries, transport, eating out) with values matching `totalsByCategory(data.json)`, and that the nav links work.
